The test image shows a tomato stem with a white/bleached lesion and small dark bodies (sclerotia) scattered on the affected area. The right segment shows heavily affected stem tissue with white fungal material. This pattern points strongly toward a stem rot disease — likely Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot or Southern_Blight.

Now I'll view reference images across 8 classes.

Now I have enough evidence to make my assessment.

**Summary of analysis:**

**Test image features:**
- Close-up of tomato stem (held in hand)
- White/bleached lesion on the stem with numerous small dark bodies (sclerotia)
- Right stem segment shows advanced infection with extensive white material and dark specks
- Black background typical of Bugwood extension photography

**Reference comparison:**
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (Bugwood_16): Showed characteristic large black sclerotia on white tissue — the dark bodies in the test image match this pattern, though smaller-looking at this scale
- **Southern_Blight** (Bugwood_2): Showed white mycelium on stem near base, but without the prominent bleached pith/stem tissue and scattered dark sclerotia
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**: Dark brown/black canker — does not match the white bleached appearance
- **Gray_Mold**: Fruit-based gray fluffy rot — not matching
- **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots**: Microscopic sporangia — not matching

The white-bleached stem tissue with small dark sclerotia embedded in it is the hallmark of Sclerotinia sclerotiorum (timber rot/white mold). Southern Blight is possible but its sclerotia are typically tan/brown (mustard-seed-like) and the reference images don't show this pattern.
